statements.text: The E-Payments User Protection Guidelines use the term 'recklessness' (paragraph 5.2). They do not use the term 'gross negligence'.
statements.note: Checked: 'gross negligence' does not appear in the 16 Dec 2024 text; 'negligence' appears once, in 5.5(a), about the institution.

statements.text: The Guidelines give examples of recklessness in footnote 20:
statements.note: Followed by footnote 20 printed from the corpus (brief 4d).

statements.text: Under paragraph 5.6 the account holder is not liable for the first S$1,000 of a loss arising from a third party's action or omission. That protection does not apply where the loss arises from an account user's failure to comply with a duty in Section 3.
statements.note: The paragraph says '$1,000' and 'any third party not referred to in paragraph 5.5'.

statements.text: Under paragraph 5.2 the account holder is liable for the actual loss where an account user's recklessness was the primary cause of the loss, up to any applicable transaction or daily payment limit agreed with the institution.

Under paragraphs 5.4 and 5.5 the account holder is not liable for a loss arising from the institution's fraud or negligence, its non-compliance with a requirement imposed by MAS, or its non-compliance with a duty in Section 4, where the loss does not arise from an account user's failure to comply with Section 3.
statements.note: 5.5(a) also names the institution's employee, agent and outsourcing service provider; 5.5(b) its employee.

statements.text: Under paragraph 7.7 the institution's report of the outcome of a disputed investigation gives the reasons for the outcome, which could include how an account user may have been reckless or may not have complied with a duty in Section 3.
statements.note: Reworded from the brief: 7.7 is the report on a disputed investigation (Section 7), and 7.7(b) says the reasons 'could include' how an account user may have been reckless.

statements.text: Section 5 of the Guidelines does not apply to credit, charge or debit card transactions (paragraph 5.1). For those the Guidelines refer to the ABS Code of Practice for Banks – Credit Cards (footnote 3).
statements.note: Both clauses are cited as not applying to cards (exclusion flag, migration 20261203120000); their scope is accounts and e-wallets.

statements.text: Paragraph 2.1 of the E-Payments User Protection Guidelines says 'high-risk activities' 'include, but are not limited to' adding payees, increasing transaction limits, disabling transaction notifications and changing the account holder's contact information. Paragraph 4.7 sets a cooling off period of at least 12 hours, when a digital security token is activated on a device, in which high-risk activities cannot be performed. The Guidelines do not name any other activity.
statements.note: Review wording (Decision 9), unchanged. Checked against mas.eupg 16 Dec 2024: 2.1 lists the four activities in longer form; 4.7 also covers a login on a new device to an account issued by a relevant payment service provider, which the draft leaves out. No other EUPG paragraph names a high-risk activity. Decision 4 prints this in card-only cases; for cards 4.7 does not apply (4.1), so a card revision would cite 4.7 as an exclusion or be split. For Elena. applies_to_instrument follows the manifest scopes loaded today; the EUPG scope table (Decision 3) is with Elena and may change it.

statements.text: Paragraph 4.7 is in Section 4 of the Guidelines. Under paragraph 4.1, Section 4 does not apply in respect of credit, charge or debit cards, except paragraphs 4.2 to 4.6, 4.10 to 4.12 and 4.14 to 4.16.
statements.note: Review wording, unchanged; matches 4.1, which speaks of cards issued by the institution. Both clauses cited as not applying to cards (exclusion flag), as eupg.fault.cards. If the scope table moves 4.1 to all payments, 4.1 can no longer be an exclusion here (in the scope-change list for Elena).

statements.text: Section 8 of the E-Payments User Protection Guidelines has applied since 16 June 2025. Paragraph 8.1 says that where an account holder reports a suspected unauthorised transaction, the institution should withhold or waive the requirement to settle the disputed amount and the charges directly relating to it until it completes its investigation. Paragraph 8.2 says the same, where the account holder does not agree with the institution's assessment, for 30 calendar days after the institution informs the account holder of the outcome, and while dispute resolution with FIDReC is under way.
statements.note: Review wording, unchanged. Differences for Elena: the text says 'withhold and/or waive' and speaks of the outstanding amount of the disputed transaction; 8.2 applies where the institution assessed the transaction as authorised or the account holder as liable and the account holder disagrees; its periods are worded more fully (from completing the investigation; from when the institution is aware FIDReC dispute resolution started, to its completion or closure). 1.5 dates the Section 8 amendments from 16 June 2025. Section 8 covers cards on the text (scope table), so sg_card would be added after confirmation. applies_to_instrument follows the manifest scopes loaded today; the EUPG scope table (Decision 3) is with Elena and may change it.

statements.text: For a disputed transaction made using a credit card or other unsecured credit facility, paragraphs 8.3 and 8.4 say the institution should ensure that the account holder's credit records with licensed credit bureaus are not adversely affected because of the disputed transaction, during the periods those paragraphs set out.
statements.note: Review wording; the text says 'due to' where the draft says 'because of'. The draft does not restate the periods; 8.4(b) is worded differently from 8.2(b) (wording sent to Elena privately). PLACEHOLDER SCOPE: meant for credit cards and other unsecured credit facilities, but 8.3/8.4 are loaded today as account_transfer + ewallet, so the approval check allows only those; account_transfer stands in for an unsecured credit facility drawn by transfer. After the scope table is confirmed this becomes sg_card (with an account-type check: debit cards are not credit). Not for approval until then. applies_to_instrument follows the manifest scopes loaded today; the EUPG scope table (Decision 3) is with Elena and may change it.

statements.text: Footnotes 26 and 27 say the institution is not obligated to do so where the disputed transactions do not fall within the scope of unauthorised transactions set out in footnote 4.
statements.note: Review wording, unchanged. 'Do so' stands for the two duties: fn26 (settling the amount and charges, 8.2 periods) and fn27 (credit records, 8.4 periods).
